title: A Fan Corrected Blizzard's Lore and Got Put Into WoW
hook: At BlizzCon 2010 a fan in a red shirt told Chris Metzen that Falstad Wildhammer was alive, and he was right. Blizzard answered with an NPC called the Wildhammer Fact Checker. Have you ever caught a game getting its own lore wrong?
script: Did you know a fan in a red shirt once corrected Blizzard's own lore team, and got written into World of Warcraft for it? At BlizzCon 2010, a Warcraft lore panel opened the floor to questions. A fan named Ian Bates stepped up to the microphone. He had just read the novel The Shattering, which seated the dwarf Falstad Wildhammer on the new Council of Three Hammers. But in the Cataclysm beta, a different dwarf named Kurdran held that seat, and Falstad was nowhere in the game. So he asked what happened to him. Chris Metzen, who had shaped Warcraft's story for years, replied that Falstad was dead. Bates calmly corrected him, and the room realized the fan was right. Lead world designer Alex Afrasiabi thanked him and promised a fix. The clip went viral, passing two million views on YouTube within a week and three million soon after. Blizzard then did something better than an apology. When Cataclysm launched in December 2010, Falstad was back on the council. Standing beside him was a brand new dwarf called the Wildhammer Fact Checker, wearing a red shirt. Bates has gone back to BlizzCon to ask more questions ever since. Have you ever caught a game getting its own story wrong? Follow for more gaming history.
